classification.tone: Gritty, claustrophobic, savage, and increasingly deranged

evaluation.positioning_hook: A newlywed couple leasing a remote house from a devout young landlord discover he’s a scarred killer with a scripture-soaked code — and the house itself is part of the trap.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The premise is instantly legible as a survival horror setup with a clean home-invasion engine and a strong central villain. The audience promise is clear, though the extremity of the violence and the religious extremity narrow the lane toward genre buyers rather than broad four-quadrant play.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The hook lands early in the opening domestic abuse sequence, then sharpens when Luke is revealed as the polite, scripture-driven landlord of the isolated house. The rules of the trap, the remote setting, and the couple-versus-host dynamic are easy to track.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Luke is the standout: a childlike, hyper-controlled zealot whose tenderness and brutality keep colliding in the same scene. Brian and Leanne are functional survivors with a workable marital dynamic, but the script is most alive when it’s using them as pressure points against Luke’s psychology.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The script commits to a nasty moral universe where hospitality, faith, and family language are weaponized. The dog, the lasagne dinner, the electrified house, and the final bait-and-switch around Leanne’s seduction give the material a confident, nasty inventiveness.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The story keeps turning the screw: the lease, the overnight stay, the electrified exits, the mutilated dog, the freezer reveal, and the forest chase all escalate cleanly. The back half is especially propulsive once the couple is trapped and forced into survival tactics.

resonant_originality.reasoning: A remote-house thriller is familiar territory, but the specific fusion of evangelical language, child abuse trauma, and a predator who performs innocence gives it a sharper identity. The final reveal that Luke has been hunting and herding them through the property gives the premise a satisfying inevitability.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: The house, boiler room, and surrounding woods are textured enough to feel story-generating, especially with the hidden basement, the clippings, and the electrified perimeter. The world is still mostly a contained pressure cooker rather than a larger social ecosystem.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The script has a very specific tonal signature: pastoral calm curdling into domestic sadism, then into scripture-fueled body horror and survival panic. The contrast between Luke’s boyish politeness and the grotesque violence around him is distinctive and hard to mistake for another script.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: There are deeper currents here around abuse, religious conditioning, and the hunger to be parented, and Luke’s scars and fixation on family suggest more beneath the surface. The script keeps that material mostly in service of the thriller engine rather than fully opening it up.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: The Brian/Leanne marriage gives the feature a solid two-hander spine, and Luke’s shifting need for mother/father figures creates a strong triangle. Beyond that, the supporting world is mostly functional and the story lives primarily on the central trio.

casting_characteristics: Luke requires a young adult actor who can play boyish innocence and physical menace
Brian requires a performer with a visible physical impairment
Leanne requires a strong dramatic lead with erotic, maternal, and survival registers
Luke appears in childhood in the opening, but the script otherwise centers an adult version of the character

locations.interior_exterior_ratio: Mostly interior with key exterior forest and driveway sequences
notable_requirements: Surrounding woods for chase and tracking sequences

technical.vfx_details: No meaningful VFX; the horror is driven by performance and practical staging.
technical.sfx_needs: Practical blood effects, corpse and body-part effects, mutilated dog reveal, electrocution gag, knife and hammer violence, freezer contents, and a hanging corpse image.

platform_fit.recommended_lane: Streaming horror, premium cable genre, or low-to-mid budget theatrical genre lane
platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model: festival-to-platform or genre-theatrical with strong trailer moments and a contained footprint

cost.note: Contemporary, contained to a small number of practical locations, with no VFX-heavy set pieces.

cast.note: The project hinges on three strong lead performances, including a physically specific Luke and a lead with an impairment.

location.note: The house, basement, and woods are manageable, but the remote setting and night forest chase add logistical complexity.

content.note: Child abuse, murder, mutilation, body horror, and religious extremity push this firmly into mature territory.

rights.note: No real people or licensed IP are central to the story; the named brands are incidental.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Luke is a nightmare lead role.
strengths.what_it_means: The script gives an actor a rare villain-protagonist showcase: childlike, seductive, devout, and physically terrifying in the same role. That’s catnip for prestige-horror buyers and for actors looking for a breakout part that can pivot from innocence to menace on a dime.
strengths.evidence: Luke’s breakfast-table politeness, the dog confrontation, the freezer reveal, and the final forest pursuit all show the same character flipping registers without warning.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The house is an active trap.
strengths.what_it_means: This is more than a location; it becomes the engine of the feature, with electrified exits, hidden spaces, and domestic routines turned into survival mechanics. Buyers like contained thrillers because they read as producible and trailer-friendly, and this one has a clear, marketable box to build inside.
strengths.evidence: The electrified door, the hidden boiler room, the trapdoor, and the way Luke controls food, water, and movement all make the house itself part of the threat.

strengths.what_it_means: The script turns ordinary couple behavior — breakfast, cleaning, laundry, sex, fostering talk — into escalating dread, which gives the movie a memorable hook beyond simple slasher mechanics. That kind of intimate escalation is attractive to buyers who want genre material with adult relationship texture.
strengths.evidence: The lasagne dinner, the dog-as-child argument, the shower and toiletry scenes, and the fostering conversation all weaponize ordinary domesticity.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Leanne has a strong final-act weapon.
strengths.what_it_means: Her seduction of Luke in the woods is the kind of reversal that gives the climax a fresh, actor-driven turn instead of a standard run-and-scream finish. That’s the sort of sequence that can sell a lead actress on the role and give the movie a memorable trailer beat.
strengths.evidence: Leanne pivots from terrified captive to manipulator, using Luke’s need for mothering and desire to be seen as a man against him.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The faith language is weaponized, not decorative.
strengths.what_it_means: The religious material isn’t window dressing; it shapes Luke’s code, his punishments, and his idea of family, which gives the script a sharper identity in the horror marketplace. That makes it appealing to genre buyers who want a moral universe with rules, not just random violence.
strengths.evidence: Luke’s scripture quotations, the “decently and in order” message, the purification language, and the Pastor Caius backstory all drive the action.

whats_special.headline: HAVEN is a contained, nasty, highly sellable horror feature with a memorable central villain and a house that behaves like a weapon. It has the kind of clean, trailer-ready escalation producers can package around a breakout lead performance and a modest practical-effects budget.

lead_characters.name: Luke
lead_characters.hook: Luke is a beautiful, damaged zealot who performs innocence like a language he learned to survive in. He can be boyish, needy, flirtatious, and then instantly feral; the scars on his body and the scripture in his mouth make him feel like a victim who became his own doctrine.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role Michael Shannon had in Take Shelter and Jack Gleeson had in Game of Thrones — a character whose stillness and sudden volatility do the heavy lifting. An actor gets to play wounded child, false prophet, and physical predator in one part, with a full-body transformation built into the writing.

lead_characters.name: Leanne Jackson
lead_characters.hook: Leanne is the sharper half of a marriage that has already survived damage, disappointment, and compromise. She reads as worldly next to Luke, but the script keeps revealing her appetite, intelligence, and capacity for ruthless improvisation when survival demands it.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Toni Collette in Hereditary or Jodie Comer in Killing Eve — a role that can move from domestic realism to feral survival strategy without losing emotional credibility. Mid-career actresses looking for a prestige genre lead will see a part with seduction, fear, maternal instinct, and violence all in one arc.

lead_characters.name: Brian Jackson
lead_characters.hook: Brian is a soft, self-conscious man trying to rebuild his life and marriage while carrying the visible evidence of a past crash. He’s vulnerable, funny, and eager to please, which makes him a perfect target for Luke’s manipulation and a compelling counterweight to Leanne’s harder edge.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of grounded, wounded lead territory Paul Walter Hauser had in Black Bird or Bryan Cranston had in Breaking Bad’s domestic scenes — a man whose fragility becomes dramatic currency. Character actors who can play decency under pressure will be drawn to the emotional humiliation, the physical limitation, and the eventual fight-for-life payoff.

lead_characters.name: Pastor Caius
lead_characters.hook: Pastor Caius is the polished face of spiritual authority turned predatory, a man whose calm language hides domination and cruelty. He functions as the ideological father behind Luke’s damage, and his presence lingers as the source of the house’s original corruption.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gave Ralph Fiennes in Schindler’s List or Michael Emerson in Lost their sinister authority — a polished, intelligent antagonist whose menace comes from control rather than volume. Actors who specialize in elegant villainy will be attracted to the chance to embody the origin point of the film’s moral rot.

lead_characters.name: MOTHER
lead_characters.hook: Luke’s mother is a feral, alcoholic parent whose cruelty is casual and absolute. She’s less a full character than a brutalizing force in Luke’s origin story, but she gives the opening a shocking domestic baseline that explains the boy’s fracture.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of small but unforgettable abusive-parent role that actors like Patricia Clarkson or Melissa Leo have turned into scene-stealing damage portraits. It offers a performer a single, concentrated burst of degradation and menace that can define the film’s emotional starting point.

lead_characters.name: FATHER
lead_characters.hook: Luke’s father is a bloated, drunken brute whose violence is impulsive, humiliating, and constant. He’s the first embodiment of the world Luke is trying to escape and later replicate in a twisted, purified form.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of brutal, lived-in menace that actors like Stephen Root or Shea Whigham can make unforgettable in a handful of scenes. The role gives a performer a hard-edged opening statement that sets the film’s moral stakes immediately.

director_appeal.hook: A director who wants to turn a contained house into a moral pressure cooker.
director_appeal.fit_profile: First- or second-feature genre directors, or established indie directors looking to pivot into horror, especially those with a taste for performance-forward suspense and practical effects. The material rewards directors who like to stage dread through blocking, silence, and behavioral shifts rather than spectacle.
director_appeal.detail: The script gives a director a clean escalation ladder: domestic unease, contained captivity, then forest pursuit. It’s the kind of material that lets a filmmaker show control over tone, actor performance, and practical horror imagery in a way that can travel from festival programmers to genre audiences.

buyer_appeal.lane: Contained elevated horror / premium streamer genre lane
buyer_appeal.detail: It can be packaged around one breakout villain lead and two strong adult co-leads, with no VFX dependency and a practical-effects-forward production plan. The contained footprint and high-concept trailer moments make it exportable for streamers and genre distributors who buy lean, concept-driven horror.

considerations.area: The opening is a full-length prologue.
considerations.detail: The abuse sequence is brutally effective and establishes Luke’s origin in force, but it also spends a meaningful amount of page time before the central couple arrives. One lever would be to consider how much of that material needs to play before the title card versus how much can be implied later through the clippings, scars, and Luke’s own testimony.

The scars, the clippings, the Pastor Caius reveal, and the final confession all work together, but they’re distributed across the feature in a way that keeps the mystery alive rather than fully opening it. A next pass could clarify which revelation should land first so Luke’s psychology feels even more inevitable as the pressure rises.

considerations.area: The house rules are the story engine.
considerations.detail: The electrified exits, hidden basement, food control, and water control are the mechanics that make the premise sing, so the script is already in a strong contained lane. If a producer wanted to simplify the footprint further, the version of the house where one fewer hidden space is needed would preserve the tension while trimming build complexity.

The story is built around three lead roles and a small number of functional supporting parts, which keeps casting and scheduling manageable. That makes the project attractive to buyers who want a contained genre package rather than an ensemble-dependent production.

considerations.area: The final seduction is the freshest turn.
considerations.detail: Leanne’s move on Luke in the woods is the most surprising character beat in the script and gives the climax a memorable psychological reversal. A next pass could protect that sequence as the emotional apex of the feature, because it’s the moment that most clearly differentiates the movie from a standard escape thriller.
